Dissolution Of Marriage.
 This Appeal, Coming On For Hearing, This Day

,
Vijaykumar A Patil J., Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal has been filed under Section 19(1) of the Family Courts Act, 1984 against the judgment dated 30.04.2016 passed in M.C.No.47/2013 by the Family Court, Shivamogga, by which the petition filed by the respondent/husband seeking dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty and desertion, has been allowed and the respondent husband is directed to pay Rs.5.00 lacs to the appellant wife towards permanent alimony.

2. Facts giving rise to filing of this appeal in brief are, marriage between appellant and respondent was solemnized on 21.05.2003 at Shivamogga and out of the wedlock appellant wife gave birth to a male child on 28.02.2004 at her parents house.

The respondent husband had requested the appellant wife to join the matrimonial home and accordingly, she came back and stayed with the respondent husband hardly for three months, and abruptly left the matrimonial home without his consent.
Despite several attempts, she refused to come and join the respondent.
Hence, the respondent husband filed petition under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, (for short 'the Act') for dissolution of marriage.

The appellant wife filed complaint against the respondent husband and his family members for the offence punishable under Section 498A, 506 r/w Section 34 of the IPC and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961, they have been acquitted in the said criminal case, which resulted in filing of the petition for dissolution of marriage by the respondent husband.
3. The respondent husband filed petition on 11.03.2013 seeking dissolution of marriage.
The petition averments are that petitioner and respondent got married on 21.05.2003 in Shivamogga and out of the wedlock, a male child was born.
When the child was aged 9 months, the appellant came back to the matrimonial home and stayed there only for three months and again went back to her parents house.
The respondent husband made several attempts to get her back but the appellant refused to come and join the respondent and lead marital life.

4. It was further averred by the respondent husband that several proceedings were initiated against him, is suffering from thyroid related disorders and the marriage between the appellant and respondent is broken down and there is no possibility of re-union.
It was further averred that since 7 years, the appellant wife and respondent husband are living separately, which has resulted in cruelty and desertion.
5. The appellant wife has entered appearance and filed objections in which she admits initiation of earlier proceedings.
She admits the place and date of marriage, but denied the allegations leveled against her and sought for dismissal of the petition.
6. The Family Court after framing the issues has recorded the evidence of the parties.
The appellant examined herself as RW.1 and got marked documents Exs.R1 to R11.

The Family Court on the basis of pleading and evidence of both the parties, by judgment dated 30.04.2016 was pleased to allow the petition for dissolution of marriage and further directed the respondent husband to pay Rs.5.00 lacs to the appellant towards permanent alimony.
7. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant wife.
Though the respondent husband is served has remained unrepresented.
8. Learned counsel for the appellant has reiterated the averments made in the statement of objections.

Learned counsel for the appellant has filed memo dated 16.02.2023 stating that appellant does not press the finding and judgment of the Family Court on dissolution of marriage,
since the respondent husband is remarried.
He confines this appeal only with regard to challenge to quantum of permanent alimony.
The said memo is taken on record.

9. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant wife is entitled for permanent alimony of Rs.25.00 lacs as she has no independent source of income, she is entirely dependant upon her parents and is required to maintain herself and also take care of the minor child, his educational and other expenses.

He further contented that as per the partition deed dated 03.02.2012, the respondent husband was allotted residential building and is owning a stationary shop, by which he is earning sufficient income.
10. We have considered the submissions of the Appellant and perused the material on record.

On the issue of grant of permanent alimony, the respondent husband has pleaded and adduced evidence that he is not doing business and as per the partition only 221 sq.ft of the property is allotted to his share and except this property, no other property is available to him.
Per Contra, the appellant wife has specifically contended that it is the respondent husband, who has the stationary shop and in addition to that, he has immovable properties.
Considering available evidence, the Family Court has directed the respondent husband to pay Rs.5.00 lacs to the appellant wife towards permanent alimony.
11. Thus, from the evidence on record, we have to ascertain whether the award of permanent alimony is required to be enhanced as pleaded by the appellant.
The parties have not led much oral and documentary evidence with respect to income, expenditure, standard of living etc., before the trial Court.

For fixing the permanent alimony payable to the appellant wife, we need to take into account the material on record, we are required to consider the age of the appellant wife and also the fact that the child born out of the wedlock is in the custody of the appellant wife, therefore, a reasonable amount of permanent alimony is required to be fixed keeping in mind the cost of living.
A careful and just balance is required to be drawn taking into account all relevant factors stated supra.

A fixed amount of alimony must be reasonable and realistic, as the appellant wife has no independent income, she is fully depending and residing with her parents and is required to take care of her minor son, his personal and educational expenses etc.
The trail Court has not considered these facts while arriving at the conclusion in fixing Rs.5,00,000/- as permanent alimony, which is very meager keeping in mind, the present day cost of living.

The finding of trial Court insofar as the fixing of quantum of permanent alimony is required to be interfered and accordingly, we deem it Sushma vs Nataraja M.M on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/171408147/

The impugned judgment and decree dated 30.04.2016 passed in M.C.No.47/2013 passed by the Family Court, Shivamogga, is modified only to extent of directing the respondent husband to pay Rs.10.00 lacs to the appellant wife towards permanent alimony.
